title: Who are the Humanitarian Decision Makers?
html:
How many times have you heard or read it: “This product will support decision makers” or some variation of that message? I have encountered it countless times over the past few years. In proposals, product fact sheets, websites, sales pitches, conferences, panels, and so on. It has become a bit of a pet peeve of mine.

I have started asking people: “Great, but which decision maker(s) exactly?”. At that point I often notice that I have startled the person and they struggle to provide a concrete answer. It has become obvious that we use this phrase “for decision makers” without really knowing who we mean and thus what they actually need. I speculate that we use this phrase to please donors or other funding mechanisms in order to justify our work. Thankfully they have not been asking for details….yet. Soon they will figure out what we are doing and will start asking the hard questions: For which decision makers?, For which decisions?, etc.

But defining decision makers and their needs is a difficult business. Over the past year, I have been collaborating with great academics like Jarrod Goentzel, from MIT Humanitarian Innovation Lab,  who is a decision making expert in the humanitarian logistics arena and Bartel Van de Walle, from ISCRAM, who is a sense making expert. We ran a work shop focusing on international (operational) responders in the first two weeks of an emergency last autumn with a report coming out soon. Internally, I polled OCHA assistants last year to see what our HQ senior managers need to know in the early phases on an emergency (resulting in an internal document of questions).

During this work, it became painfully clear how large and diverse the range of decision makers are in humanitarian response. In an effort to define out these decision makers in a generalized fashion, I have started working with Quentin Nicaise to develop a first draft of a Decision Makers Taxonomy. It will be generalized down to roles within different organization types and locations. We will work with Jarrod and Bartel to incorporate their expert opinions and will then open it up widely for comment. We aim to release a first version in August. Hopefully the community will grab this work and continue to improve and refine it well beyond August. It could become a hugely valuable resource especially when the next layer (what each decision maker role generally needs to know) is added!

If you are interested to get involved, leave me a comment. If you are interested to get periodic updates by email, subscribe to my blog.

Andrej
teaser: Which decision makers? A pet peeve about products 'for decision makers', and a workshop with Jarrod Goentzel and Bartel Van de Walle to define them.
seo_description: Why the phrase 'support decision makers' is too vague, and work towards a clearer view of humanitarian decision makers.
